\caption{\textbf{Progressive \sca{} beats every single-pass baseline on all ten per-image metrics and pays in patch FID.} Expands the progressive row of Table~\ref{tab:main}. FLUX.1-dev at $4096^2$, \nmain{} Aesthetic-4K prompts, seed 0. Each cell is progressive \sca{} minus the row's method, with its 95\% paired interval below it in grey: 2000 prompt draws for the per-image metrics, and for FID, KID, and their patch versions 1000 draws that also resample the 168 reference-image clusters. $^{\times}$: $\times100$; $^{\ast}$: $\times1000$. \up{Blue} / \dn{orange}: the interval excludes zero in favour of / against progressive \sca{}; for FID and KID lower is better, so a negative difference is a gain. Inception score has no paired interval (Table~\ref{tab:all_metrics}); Table~\ref{tab:holm} gives the Holm-adjusted calls. The point estimate lies outside its percentile interval for Full attn. patch FID, as it can for a biased statistic. Key result: progressive \sca{} is significantly better than AReA, DyPE, SEGA, and full attention on every per-image metric and than UltraImage on nine; its differences from HRDiT on ImageReward, HPSv2.1, and PickScore include zero, and its patch FID is higher than AReA's, HRDiT's, and single-pass \sca{}'s.}
